dialogues.text_a: Can you operate a centre lathe machine?
dialogues.text_b: No, I can’t. But I can use a bench grinder.

dialogues.text_a: Can Ruwan assemble mechanical components accurately?
dialogues.text_b: Of course, he can. He assembles mechanical components every day. He’s a mechanical trainee.

dialogues.text_a: When are you going to measure the shaft diameter?
dialogues.text_b: I’m going to measure it tomorrow morning.

dialogues.text_a: When is Ravi going to replace the worn bearing?
dialogues.text_b: He might replace it this morning, or he might replace it this afternoon. He really doesn’t know.
Sunil is not feeling very well. He has a pain in wrist.
dialogues.text_c: Pain in his wrist? How did he get it?
dialogues.text_d: He tightened bolts with a spanner all day yesterday.

dialogues.text_a: Did you align the coupling correctly yesterday afternoon?
dialogues.text_b: No, I didn’t. I was feeling too tired.

dialogues.text_a: Why did you lubricate the guide rails this morning?
dialogues.text_b: I lubricated them to reduce friction.

dialogues.text_a: I bought a new cutting tool yesterday.
dialogues.text_b: Really? But I liked your old cutting tool. It was sharp.
dialogues.text_c: That’s true. But my new cutting tool is sharper.

dialogues.text_a: Why are you checking the machine alignment right now?
dialogues.text_b: I’m checking the alignment now because I checked it yesterday, but it was incorrect. I am going to operate the machine this afternoon, and I might use it again later.
I am upset because I have to redo the measurement. I always check the dimensions before machining, but this morning I forgot, and it was a careless mistake.

dialogues.text_c: That’s unusual. Do you usually clean the machine bed now?
dialogues.text_d: No, I usually clean it after work, but I am cleaning it now.
dialogues.text_f: Because there is too much metal dust on it.

dialogues.text_a: Can you and Amal start the milling operation now?
dialogues.text_b: No, we can’t. We have to finish setting the workpiece first.

content.text: to adjust a tool or machine so it measures or works accurately.
to put a part or component into position so it can operate correctly.
to find the cause of a mechanical or electrical problem.
to check a system step by step to identify and fix faults.
to position parts so they are straight, level, and working in the correct orientation.
to turn or spin a part around a central point.
to apply oil or grease to reduce friction between moving parts.
to increase the speed of a vehicle.
to remove air from a system, such as brake lines, so the fluid can flow properly.

activity_c.text: Today I want to talk about how you are handling safety procedures and maintenance tasks in the mechanical workshop.
For example, the lathe-machine check took longer than expected.
Yesterday the main shaft was tighter than usual, and I had to readjust the bearings twice.
The alignment was also more uneven than I thought.
I’m going to inspect the tool post and test the emergency stop button.
I must also record everything in the daily maintenance log, because the administration team needs clear reports.
Are you checking the PPE rack regularly?
I check it every evening, but yesterday I wasn’t able to finish the face-shield sanitizing step.
